verdict.line: You win if you force all-ins at levels 3-8 before Nasus stacks Siphoning Strike and lands Wither; you lose if the lane drags past 20 minutes and he hits a stacked Fury of the Sands.

brief.thesis: Nasus's Q (Siphoning Strike, cooldown 8/7/6/5/4s, range 255) permanently gains damage every time it kills a unit, so he starts weak and his entire power curve is just how many minions and champions he's been allowed to farm with it. Jax's E (Counter Strike, cooldown 18/16/14/12/10s) dodges all incoming basic attacks for its duration and then stuns, which directly shuts down Nasus's auto-reliant trading and Soul Eater lifesteal. Every minute you let him free-farm resets the clock in his favor - this is a lane you're built to win now, not later.

theirWindow.when: After he lands Wither on you
theirWindow.what: Wither (W, cooldown 15/14/13/12/11s, range 700) decelerates your Movement and Attack Speed over time, which guts your R (Relentless Assault) stacking attacks and your ability to chase. Don't commit to the all-in once it's on you - disengage and let it burn off before re-engaging.

yourWindow.what: Use Q (Leap Strike) to close the gap, W (Empower) on the follow-up hit for burst, and E (Counter Strike) to dodge his autos and stun him. His only tool at this point is a short-range Q with no CC, so you win every clean engage.

powerCurve.note: Neither all-in kit fully online yet
Empower and Counter Strike win trades
Stacked Siphoning Strike snowballs his trades
Fury of the Sands outscales you

start.why: The highest-picked start (71.6% pick, 45.5% WR over 101 games) - the extra damage and sustain let you actually close out the levels 3-5 all-in windows instead of poking and backing off.

boots.why: Picked over Mercury's Treads here (42.3% pick vs 36.2%) because Nasus's whole early kit - Soul Eater lifesteal and auto-reliant Siphoning Strike - is basic-attack damage, which Steelcaps directly reduces.

core.why: The most-picked, highest-winning core path (66.7% WR into this build) - the on-hit damage and movement speed let you force fights before he stacks up.
Second item in the top core path; the proc rewards exactly the short burst trades E (Counter Strike) sets up.
Closes out the top core path and gives you a way to survive the one thing that scales against you - his stacked Fury of the Sands damage in a skirmish.

situational.when: he's farmed enough Q to stack into a tanky late game, since its current-health damage ignores whatever health stacking he's built up
the lane goes long and you need sustain to outlast his Soul Eater lifesteal in extended trades
the game drags past 20 minutes and you need a stat item to keep pace with his late-game scaling

runes.keystoneWhy: The attack speed ramp rewards the extended auto-trades your E (Counter Strike) sets up and synergizes directly with R (Relentless Assault)'s every-third-hit bonus - it's the higher-pick-rate page (36.5%) for a reason.

summoners.why: The most-picked combo (69.1% pick) and it matches your actual advantage here - the data shows a solo-kill edge for Jax, and Ignite seals those levels 3-8 all-ins through his Soul Eater lifesteal. Swap to Teleport if you'd rather use your lane lead to pressure side waves than force kills.

playing.title: All-in before level 6
playing.detail: Before Nasus hits 6 and unlocks Fury of the Sands (R, cooldown 120s), his only tool is Siphoning Strike - short range, no CC, and a real cooldown. Leap in with Q, land W (Empower), and win it clean.

playing.title: Trade through Counter Strike
playing.detail: Walk into his auto range and pop E - you dodge all incoming basic attacks for its duration, then stun him. This nullifies his autos and Soul Eater lifesteal entirely, and it's the matchup's own stated read for a reason.

playing.title: Contest every CS he Qs
playing.detail: Siphoning Strike permanently gains damage every time it kills a unit, so each minion he last-hits is a permanent stat gain. Shove the wave and force him off farm during your levels 3-8 lead to deny that stacking.

playing.title: Back off once Wither lands
playing.detail: Wither decelerates your Movement and Attack Speed over time once it hits, which kills your R's attack-speed stacking and your chase. Reset instead of forcing a slowed-down fight.

playing.title: Don't stand in Spirit Fire
playing.detail: Spirit Fire (E, cooldown 12s, range 650) reduces the Armor of anyone standing in it, which buffs his auto and Q damage against you - step out of the zone before trading.

playing.title: Convert the lane lead into tempo
playing.detail: The head-to-head win rate is only 44.5% over 110 games despite Jax holding lane and solo-kill advantage - that gap is games where the lane win doesn't turn into a game win. Take plates and towers off your kills instead of farming toward a late-game fantasy.

playing.title: Burst him fast in skirmishes after 6
playing.detail: Fury of the Sands grants him bonus Health, Attack Range, and drains nearby enemies' max Health as bonus damage for its duration - any fight that goes long past his ult cast is one he's built to win. Front-load your damage instead of extending the trade.

brief.patchCaveat: The build paths, rune pages, and the 44.5% head-to-head win rate over 110 games are measured from live op.gg data on the current patch; the mechanical reasoning behind them - why the lane swings this way - is my own read.

stats.opponentTip: Use Counter Strike [E] to block Nasus’s basic attacks while fighting him.
